main_text.p: qua, ˇ sub. Cæteræ vocales sæpius levigantur. Sed nota levis spiritus inutilis videtur, cúm intelligatur ubi asper desit.

Veteres etiam in medio spiritum addebant, ut ὤεχος manfuetus, πεως pavo: ut Latini in mihi & mehe. Æoles omnino nihil aspirāt: inde ἄμμες pro ἡμεῖς, nos: ὑμμες per ὑμεῖς, vos: ἀπλω pro ἁπλω, apto, necto.
E confonis quatuor aspirantur: ῥῶ semper initio dictionis, ut ῥώμη robur.
Quidam excipiunt ἐχεος robustus, venter: ἐχειας Rarias, Cereris epitheton apud Suidam: ἐχειον puer, ῥωεος vehemens, propter ρ geminatum. Sed Æolum videntur hæc nihil aspirantium.
In medio simplex tenuatur, nec ullo spiritu notatur, ut illa ἐχειας, ἐχειον.

page.notes: Greek words are only approximately legible in this scan: the breathings, accents and some letters of ἄμμες, ὑμμες, ἐχεος, ἐχειας, ἐχειον, ῥωεος, ὤεχος and πεως are uncertain and should be checked against the original. The word "ˇ" after "qua," is a small Greek accent mark that is not fully legible. Several Greek words in the scan are blurred by stains.
